entries.clue: Asian ape Jane’s disturbed (8)

indicatorNotes.disturbed: letters that are disturbed are thrown out of order

annotation.surface: Jane is rattled by an ape somewhere in Asia.
annotation.walkthrough: The apostrophe is surface dressing: its S is simply one of the fodder letters.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the adjective for the people and things of Japan, an Asian country.

entries.clue: A place for thieves in port? (4)

blocks.note: the proverbial lair where robbers gather

annotation.surface: A riddle asking where a port's thieves hang out.
annotation.walkthrough: Read as a whole it sounds like a cryptic definition of a criminal harbour; split it after 'thieves' and it is A + DEN. Aden is a port in Yemen.
annotation.definitionFit: Aden is a major seaport in Yemen.

entries.clue: Soldier needing some plan, certainly (6)

indicatorNotes.needing some: the answer needs only some of the letters that follow

blocks.note: the letters straddle the comma, from the second letter of plan to the fourth of certainly

annotation.surface: A soldier certainly needs something of a plan.
annotation.walkthrough: The comma is ignored: the answer runs across it.
annotation.definitionFit: A lancer is a cavalry soldier armed with a lance.

entries.clue: Apt to scratch items of clothing I have, source of annoyance initially (8)

annotation.surface: Scratchy garments that irritate their owner.
annotation.walkthrough: The last piece of wordplay goes first in the answer: A leads, then BRAS, then I'VE.
annotation.definitionFit: Something abrasive scratches or scrapes a surface.

entries.clue: Gosh, old country offers occasion to put Union Jack bunting up! (10)

annotation.definition: occasion to put Union Jack bunting up

blocks.note: cor! is a British exclamation of surprise, like gosh

annotation.surface: Someone exclaims that the old country is putting on a show of flags.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition is a whole descriptive phrase: the Union Jack is the British flag, and a coronation is when streets are strung with it.
annotation.definitionFit: British coronations are celebrated with streets hung in Union Jack bunting.

entries.clue: Worker retained by stars in shed (4-2)

indicatorNotes.retained by: the first part is held inside the second

blocks.note: Leo is a constellation, a group of stars

annotation.surface: A worker kept on by star performers inside a shed.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Stars' means one constellation, not celebrities: LE(ANT)O.
annotation.definitionFit: A lean-to is a shed built against a wall.

entries.clue: Servant not associated with factory production, we hear (8)

indicatorNotes.we hear: what we hear is a sound, not a spelling

annotation.surface: A servant who has no truck with mass production.
annotation.walkthrough: A long paraphrase stands for one word, hand-made, whose sound gives the servant.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, somewhat old-fashioned: a woman who waits on a mistress.

entries.clue: Lower minister enthrals yours truly (6)

indicatorNotes.enthrals: to enthral is to hold captive, so the first part holds the second

blocks.note: a dean is a senior clergyman

annotation.surface: A junior minister captivates the setter.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Lower' looks like an adjective describing the minister; it is the verb, to demean. DE(ME)AN.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the verb sense: to degrade someone, bring them down in others' eyes.

entries.clue: Show dislike of Edward – gets kicked (6)

annotation.surface: Edward is jeered and then kicked out.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition sits at the end; 'gets' just leads into it.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: struck with a boot, the past participle matching 'kicked'.

entries.clue: European champions, not the first to bring anguish (4)

indicatorNotes.not the first: the first letter is not included

blocks.note: SPAIN, football's European champions, minus its first letter S

annotation.surface: Beaten finalists feel the anguish of the European champions.
annotation.walkthrough: The champions are a national team: Spain have won football's European Championship several times.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both words name acute suffering, of body or mind.

entries.clue: Happen regularly to modify opinion (4,6)

blocks.note: recur, as festivals do each year
be persuaded round to another view

annotation.surface: Someone changes their mind at regular intervals.
annotation.walkthrough: Two senses of one phrasal verb, joined by 'to'.
annotation.definitionFit: Recurring events come around; a persuaded person comes around.

entries.clue: Withdraw agent before broadcast (6)

indicatorNotes.before: the first part comes before the second

blocks.note: a rep is a sales agent
to air a programme is to broadcast it

annotation.surface: An agent pulls out before going on air.
annotation.walkthrough: Repair here is not 'fix' but the formal verb 'go', as in 'we repaired to the drawing room'.
annotation.definitionFit: To repair to a place is to withdraw or retire there.

entries.clue: Notice only chaps needing time to make small change (10)

annotation.surface: A notice says only the lads need time to sort out some coins.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Small change' suggests loose coins; it means a minor alteration.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a slight alteration or tweak, not loose coins.

entries.clue: Rita got disturbed, having taken in a troublemaker? (8)

indicatorNotes.disturbed: the letters are thrown out of order
indicatorNotes.having taken in: the anagram takes the next letter inside it

blocks.note: taken as it stands, slipped in after the fourth letter

annotation.surface: Rita is rattled after letting a stirrer into her circle.
annotation.walkthrough: Anagram first, then insert A: AGIT(A)TOR.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: someone who stirs up unrest, often political.

entries.clue: A collection of people in court for a crime (7)

blocks.note: a = per, as in £5 a head

annotation.surface: A jury gathered to try a crime.
annotation.walkthrough: The innocent 'A' does real work: 'a' means 'per', as in 'twice a day'. Perjury is a crime committed in court.
annotation.definitionFit: Perjury, lying under oath, is a crime.

entries.clue: Those getting left behind putting out a hint for action (8)

indicatorNotes.putting out: the named letter is put out of the word

blocks.note: REMAINDER, those left behind, with the A put out

annotation.surface: Stragglers put out a prompt to get moving.
annotation.walkthrough: The 'a' that reads as an article in 'a hint' is the letter taken from REMAINDER.
annotation.definitionFit: A reminder prompts someone to do something.

entries.clue: Times with pride so wounded (7)

indicatorNotes.wounded: the letters are damaged into a new order

annotation.surface: In certain times, pride is badly hurt.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Times' might be the newspaper; it is plural periods of time.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: stretches or eras of history.

entries.clue: Habit coming over time in part of equestrian show (8)

indicatorNotes.coming over: in a down clue, the first part sits over the second

blocks.note: a habit is a garment, as a nun's or a rider's
an age is a period of time

annotation.surface: A riding habit worn over time in a horse show.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Habit' is clothing, not routine, and fits the equestrian scene: a riding habit.
annotation.definitionFit: Dressage is the event where a horse performs set movements.

entries.clue: Grab a bit (6)

blocks.note: a fragment, as of overheard conversation

annotation.surface: Take a small piece.
annotation.walkthrough: Two words, two definitions: the verb and the noun.
annotation.definitionFit: Two senses: the verb to seize quickly, and the noun for a short fragment, as of a song.

entries.clue: Force fellows to become journalists (8)

annotation.surface: Men forced into working as reporters.
annotation.walkthrough: The pieces simply follow each other.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, dated: men who work for newspapers.

entries.clue: Monkey rushes around (6)

annotation.surface: A monkey dashes about.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Monkey' could be a verb (to monkey about); it is the animal.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: a species of macaque, familiar from medical research and the Rh blood factor.

entries.clue: Way old queen is hugged by mister (6)

indicatorNotes.is hugged by: the first part is held inside the second

blocks.note: Mr is the abbreviation of mister

annotation.surface: An old queen gets a hug from a gentleman.
annotation.walkthrough: M(ANNE)R.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a mode or fashion of doing something.

entries.clue: Sultry Maureen got up (6)

annotation.surface: A brooding Maureen gets out of bed.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Sultry' is used in its sense of sullen or gloomy, not hot or seductive.
annotation.definitionFit: Sultry can mean sullen, which is what morose means.

entries.clue: Retrain Tom possibly to be a killer (10)

indicatorNotes.possibly: the letters could possibly form something else

annotation.surface: Tom might be retrained as an assassin.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Retrain' looks like the indicator but is fodder; 'possibly' does the rearranging.
annotation.definitionFit: A terminator ends things, and the film character is a killing machine.

entries.clue: Ultimate piece of cobbler’s equipment (4)

blocks.note: the foot-shaped block a shoemaker works on

annotation.surface: The finest tool in a cobbler's kit.
annotation.walkthrough: A cobbler is a shoe repairer; the last is the foot-shaped form a shoe is built or mended on.
annotation.definitionFit: Last means ultimate, and a last is a shoemaker's form.

entries.clue: Put down, face up (4)

indicatorNotes.up: in a down clue, up means read from the bottom

blocks.note: a dial is a clock face

annotation.surface: Put down, turned face-upward.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Face up' reads as a posture; 'face' is DIAL, sent up the grid.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: past tense of lay, to set something down.

entries.clue: Fruit offered by one of five children attending church (6)

indicatorNotes.attending: one part is next to the other, in attendance

blocks.note: a quin is one of quintuplets

annotation.surface: A child from a set of quintuplets hands out fruit at church.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Attending church' reads as going to a service; it just places the two pieces side by side.
annotation.definitionFit: A quince is a hard, pear-shaped fruit.

entries.clue: Town has to keep smart (8)

indicatorNotes.to keep: the first word keeps the next inside it

annotation.surface: A town is required to retain its chic.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Smart' looks like the adjective 'stylish'; it is the verb, to sting. HA(STING)S. Hastings is a seaside town in East Sussex.
annotation.definitionFit: Hastings is a town on England's south coast.
